problem.title: Prior Auth Coverage Gap Analysis
problem.prompt: Your health plan wants to identify providers who have submitted prior authorization requests for BOTH 'MRI' AND 'CT Scan' imaging modalities but have NEVER submitted a request for 'X-Ray' during the tracking period. The goal is to offer targeted training on cost-effective X-Ray utilization to these providers. Write a query that returns the provider_id and provider_name for all qualifying providers, ordered by provider_id ascending. A provider qualifies if their authorization requests include at least one MRI AND at least one CT Scan AND zero X-Rays. Providers with no authorization requests in the system should not appear in the result.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE providers (provider_id INT PRIMARY KEY, provider_name VARCHAR(100), specialty VARCHAR(50)); CREATE TABLE prior_authorizations (auth_id INT PRIMARY KEY, provider_id INT, imaging_modality VARCHAR(50), request_date DATE, status VARCHAR(20));

composite_moves: join providers to prior_authorizations on provider_id
filter groups using CASE-based set membership checks in HAVING: BOOL_OR(imaging_modality = 'MRI') AND BOOL_OR(imaging_modality = 'CT Scan') AND NOT BOOL_OR(imaging_modality = 'X-Ray')

hints: Think about how to check whether a provider has submitted requests for specific imaging modalities using aggregate functions.
Use BOOL_OR or MAX(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) inside a HAVING clause to check for the presence or absence of each required and forbidden modality.
Group by provider and use HAVING with three conditions: one for MRI presence, one for CT Scan presence, and one for X-Ray absence (NOT BOOL_OR or MAX = 0).
problem.answer_key: SELECT p.provider_id, p.provider_name FROM providers AS p JOIN prior_authorizations AS pa ON pa.provider_id = p.provider_id GROUP BY p.provider_id, p.provider_name HAVING BOOL_OR(pa.imaging_modality = 'MRI') AND BOOL_OR(pa.imaging_modality = 'CT Scan') AND NOT BOOL_OR(pa.imaging_modality = 'X-Ray') ORDER BY p.provider_id;

user_solution:
/*
Your health plan wants to identify providers who have submitted prior authorization requests for BOTH 'MRI' AND 'CT Scan' imaging modalities but have NEVER submitted a request for 'X-Ray' during the tracking period.
Write a query that returns the provider_id and provider_name for all qualifying providers, ordered by provider_id ascending.
A provider qualifies if their authorization requests include at least one MRI AND at least one CT Scan AND zero X-Rays.
Providers with no authorization requests in the system should not appear in the result.
*/

SELECT
    p.provider_id,
    p.provider_name
FROM prior_authorizations AS pa
JOIN providers AS p
    ON p.provider_id = pa.provider_id
GROUP BY p.provider_id, p.provider_name
HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN pa.imaging_modality = 'MRI' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AND
        MAX(CASE WHEN pa.imaging_modality = 'CT Scan' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AND
        MAX(CASE WHEN pa.imaging_modality = 'X-Ray' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0
ORDER BY p.provider_id;
